title: Division: sharing vs grouping
examples: When do I know if I should share or group?
What is the difference between a remainder of zero and a remainder of one?
How does division relate to multiplication?

explain.say: Division means splitting things into equal groups. You can share, or you can make groups.
Share ten sweets between two friends. Give one sweet to each friend, again and again. Each friend gets five sweets.
Now make groups. Put ten sweets into bags, with two in each bag. Count the bags. You make five bags.
Sometimes things are left over. Share seven sweets between two friends. Each gets three, and one is left over. The one left over is called the remainder.
Division undoes multiplication. Three groups of four make twelve. So twelve shared into three groups is four each.

faq.q: When should I use sharing versus grouping?
faq.a: If the problem says sharing among people, you are sharing. If it says putting into equal groups, you are grouping. You can look for keywords to help you decide.
asks: What tells me which way to divide?

faq.q: What does a remainder of zero mean?
faq.a: A remainder of zero means that everything was shared or grouped perfectly. There are no items left over at all.
asks: Does zero remainder mean it divides exactly?
What if there are no leftovers?

faq.q: How do I check if my division is correct?
faq.a: Multiply your answer by the number you divided by. Then add anything left over. You should get the number you started with.
asks: What is the inverse of division?

faq.q: Is grouping always the same as sharing?
faq.a: Not always. Sharing is about dividing a total amount by the number of groups. Grouping is about seeing how many groups of a certain size fit into the total amount.
asks: Are sharing and grouping the same thing?
Do they always give the same answer?

faq.q: What if the remainder is bigger than the group size?
faq.a: The remainder must always be smaller than the number you are grouping by. If it is not, you have not divided completely.
asks: What is the rule for the remainder?

facts: Division can be understood as splitting a total into equal parts.
If you divide a number by itself, the answer is one. This works for every number except zero.
The remainder must always be less than the divisor.
Division is the inverse operation of multiplication.

quiz.say: Put the twelve stars in groups of three. Tap how many groups.
quiz.why: Count in threes: 3, 6, 9, 12. That is 4 groups.

wrong.1: The number 3 is how many stars go in each group.
wrong.2: The number 9 is 12 take away 3, so keep making groups until all are used.

quiz.say: Share the apples between two children. Tap what each child gets.
quiz.why: Give one apple to each child, again and again. Each child gets 3, and 1 apple is left over.

wrong.0: Four each would use 8 apples, and there are just 7.
wrong.2: With 3 left over, you can still give each child one more.

quiz.say: Tap the multiplication fact that checks this division.

options.say: twelve take away three is nine

quiz.why: 3 groups of 4 make 12. So 12 shared into 3 groups is 4 each.

wrong.0: This takes away 3 one time, and division needs equal groups.
wrong.1: This adds the numbers, and checking a division needs multiplying.
